newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Soyuz craft with two Russians undock from Mir.
newsitem.headline: Soyuz craft with two Russians undock from Mir.

text.p: A Soyuz spacecraft with two Russian cosmonauts undocked from the troubled Mir on Thursday to take them to Earth after the most gruelling mission in the space station's 11-year history.
Live television pictures at Mission Control showed Soyuz with commander Vasily Tsibliyev and flight engineer Alexander Lazutkin departing from Mir at 12:56 Moscow time (0856 GMT).

A Mission Control operator said the undocking went "normally" but there appeared to be a three-minute delay in the operation compared to the original schedule. The initial speed of Soyuz was three metres (yards) per second.
A huge screen at Mission Control showed two bright dots -- Mir and Soyuz quickly departing from each other. "It seems we are quite far from it (Mir)," Tsibliyev said.
The crew is scheduled to touch down at 1216 GMT in the ex-Soviet republic of Kazakhstan.
